chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim said: Ibn Jabala narrated to us from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a woman who performs Hajj al-Tamattuʿ, then becomes menstruating before she performs the Tawaf al-Ifadah (of the House), so she departs for ʿArafāt. He said: Her Hajj becomes a Hajj al-Qirān (or rather, the text implies the status changes, but the ruling is discussed). I said: Is there something upon her? He said: Blood that she pours, and it is her sacrifice (Uḍḥiya).

Muhammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: His (the Imam's) statement 'upon her is blood that she pours' is to be understood as recommended (istibḥāb) rather than obligatory (wujūb), because when the Tamattuʿ is lost, her Hajj becomes Mufrad, and the Mufrad is not required to offer a sacrifice, as we have clarified. This indicates what we said regarding recommendation.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابُ: Recommendation (a legal status between obligation and permissibility)
key_terms.حَجَّةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: Hajj al-Mufrad (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are combined without the specific Tamattuʿ structure, often implying different ritual requirements)
key_terms.طَوَافُ الْمُتَعَةِ: Tawaf al-Ifadah (the farewell or principal circumambulation associated with Tamattuʿ)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who menstruates before Tawaf al-Ifadah during Hajj al-Tamattuʿ?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that a woman performing Hajj al-Tamattuʿ who menstruates before Tawaf al-Ifadah converts her pilgrimage to Hajj al-Mufrad, necessitating a sacrifice (dam). Shaykh al-Tusi and later scholars like Muhammad ibn al-Hasan clarify that this 'blood' is recommended (mustaḥabb) rather than obligatory, as the primary obligation of Uḍḥiya is tied to the completion of the Tamattuʿ rites. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of adapting ritual obligations based on the specific type of Hajj performed when circumstances prevent its full completion.
